clue.text: What Spooner's horse does to bunch of flowers

indicators.note: Spooner's signals a Spoonerism: the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: what a horse does, among other things, is go: here GOES
a horse says neigh, its whinny

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a horse does to a bunch of flowers, perhaps eats it.
explanation.walkthrough: What a horse does is GOES NEIGH; Spooner swaps the opening sounds to give NOSE GAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosegay is a small posy, a traditional term for a little hand-held bouquet.

clue.text: Political extremist emerges from a zone in turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is a state of confusion, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A radical figure surfaces from a war-torn region.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' that looks like a link word is part of the fodder: A ZONE IN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi belongs to the far right, a clear example of a political extremist.

clue.text: Undermine replacement surgeon fixing radius

parts.note: a substitute player is a sub

indicators.note: fixing here means fastening something into place, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
R is the standard abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A stand-in surgeon is fixing a broken arm bone, the radius.
explanation.definitionFit: To subvert an institution is to weaken or undermine it from within.

clue.text: Yank gets upset stomach

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to yank is to tug sharply

explanation.surface: An American gets an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American; it is the verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Gut is an everyday synonym for the belly or stomach.

clue.text: Secret agent, turned and broken by the Spanish, squeals

indicators.note: broken by means split apart with another piece pushed into the gap
turned means flipped round, so the word for the agent is written backwards

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A double agent, turned and broken by Spanish interrogators, squeals to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes YPS, which EL splits after the Y. 'Squeals' looks like informing, the spy's betrayal, but it means cries out.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelps and squeals are both short high-pitched cries, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Dignified bearing with romantic partner

parts.note: SE, south-east, is a compass bearing
a date is the person you go out with romantically

explanation.surface: Someone of dignified bearing arrives with a romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dignified bearing' reads as one phrase, but 'bearing' is the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, composed and unhurried, much like dignified.

clue.text: Abandon cars precariously, if stuck on rocks

indicators.note: stuck on means attached to, so one piece is placed next to the other
precariously means unsteadily, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: in a drink served on the rocks, the rocks are ice cubes

explanation.surface: Cars abandoned, perilously perched, perhaps stuck on rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: To sacrifice something is to give it up or abandon it for another end.

clue.text: Pipe's diameter above showers

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places one piece on top of, so before, the other

parts.note: showers are falls of rain

explanation.surface: A plumbing note: the pipe's diameter is above the showers.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe or channel that carries away waste water.

clue.text: Joint currency problem

parts.note: a T-joint is a joint shaped like the letter T
the rouble is the currency of Russia

explanation.surface: A shared monetary system has run into a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint currency' suggests something like the euro, but the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a difficulty or worry, a synonym of problem.

clue.text: Burning paintings in study? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: in would put the paintings inside the study
this reverses the instruction, so the study goes inside the paintings instead

parts.note: paintings are art
a study or den is a private room for work

explanation.surface: Pictures burning in a study? The clue cheekily corrects itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, figuratively burning with feeling.

clue.text: Going round in circles, taking part in test

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: Someone sitting an exam feels they are going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital path goes round and round a body, as in a planet's circuit.

clue.text: Uproar about Dorothy, perhaps

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
Dorothy Lamour was a Hollywood star of the Road to... films

explanation.surface: A fuss breaks out over a woman named Dorothy, perhaps the Wizard of Oz heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamour is a loud, insistent outcry, much like an uproar.

clue.text: Reflecting, for example, on a period of history

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the first piece after the second
reflecting, as in a mirror, means the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone muses, for example, on a period of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' makes GE, which sits on, so after, A.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is an era, a distinct stretch of the past such as the Iron Age.

clue.text: Popular tale about Australian girl draws one in

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tale wraps round the rest

parts.note: a fable is a moral tale

indicators.note: draws with in means pulls a piece inside
with draws, means pulled inside

parts.note: Shona is a girl's name; the 'Australian' tag adds no letters, as no A is spare
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A popular yarn about an Australian girl draws one in.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter admitted on the blog that 'Australian' was a slip that should have been edited out: it would add an A the answer has no room for. 'draws ... in' adds the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashionable is in vogue, liked by many and so popular.

clue.text: Where you might find 18 is fake

definitions.meaning: an anvil, the answer to 18, stands in a smithy
to fake a signature or banknote is to counterfeit it

explanation.surface: Where you'd find an anvil is a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a blacksmith's workshop, and to forge is also to counterfeit.

clue.text: Lay to rest trendy theory, regularly expounded

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the first, third and fifth of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wants to bury a fashionable theory, set out at regular length.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, laying it to rest in a grave.

clue.text: Incomparably refined Scandinavian, say, set it in motion

indicators.note: say signals a word said aloud, here one that sounds the same as a different spelling

parts.note: a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

indicators.note: in motion means moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A refined Scandinavian sets something going.
explanation.walkthrough: DANE spoken gives DAIN; 'in motion' turns SET IT into TIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Incomparably refined is the superlative: the most delicate or dainty of all.

clue.text: Stuff gathered on shore surprisingly did for two

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Washed-up material that unexpectedly did for two people.
explanation.definitionFit: Driftwood is timber that washes up and collects on beaches.

clue.text: Write article about another feudal lord

indicators.note: about means around, so one article wraps the other

parts.note: the is the definite article
another article, the indefinite one: an

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a piece about another feudal lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write' simply tells you to put the pieces down; 'another' means a second article.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Saxon or Scottish noble holding land from the king, a feudal lord.

clue.text: Proclaim one's allegiance to America

parts.note: to state is to declare or proclaim
your side is the camp you belong to

explanation.surface: Someone declares loyalty to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allegiance to America' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'to America'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an adverb meaning in or towards the USA.

clue.text: Declared purpose sounds corrupt

indicators.note: sounds tells you the phrase is heard, not read, giving a word spoken alike

parts.note: declared means said aloud, past tense of say; a purpose is a use, as in what something is for

explanation.surface: A stated aim sounds corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce someone is to lead them astray, to corrupt them morally.

clue.text: Exonerate a bishop taking crack

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: A bishop clears someone's name after cracking the case.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to clear of guilt or blame, as exonerate means.

clue.text: One takes a pounding in German village

indicators.note: in tells you the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a beating in a German village.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a smith hammers metal on, so it is constantly struck.

clue.text: Some Scouse git's evidently up for a scrap

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
some means a portion of the words that follow, so the letters are within them

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian lout is clearly spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up for a scrap' suggests a brawl; 'scrap' is the noun meaning a trace. Scouse means from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a tiny remaining trace, a scrap or remnant of something.

clue.text: Soldier enthralled by the French Navy's old-fashioned signalling device

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: le is French for the
a soldier ant is a kind of ant
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A soldier captivated by the French Navy's antique signalling equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanterns were long used to flash signals, before radio replaced them.

clue.text: E.g. Bedouin bride dancing round street wantonly

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one set of letters encloses the other
dancing means moving about, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
wantonly means recklessly, so these letters too are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bride dances shamelessly round a street.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagram signals: 'dancing' works on the bride, 'wantonly' on the street, and 'round' wraps the first about the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are nomadic Arab peoples of the desert, an example of such a tribe.

clue.text: Regret about class or money

indicators.note: about means around, so the regret wraps the class

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
PE, physical education, is a school class

explanation.surface: Someone has regrets over class or money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and Pakistan, so a form of money.

clue.text: Setter's born with hollow urge to impregnate

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, so setter's is I'm

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: The setter was born with an empty urge to impregnate.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or steep, in the sense of impregnate meaning soak through.

clue.text: Loud-mouthed lad gets a shiner

indicators.note: loud-mouthed hints the word is spoken out, so it is heard as a word spelt differently

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son

explanation.surface: A mouthy boy gets a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shiner' looks like a black eye; it is something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun is the great shining body in our sky, a shiner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Nymph plays hard to get in company

indicators.note: get in means enter, so these letters go inside the other piece
hard here means roughly treated, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A nymph plays hard to get when others are present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays hard to get' reads as an idiom; 'hard' scrambles PLAYS into ALYPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Calypso is the sea nymph of the Odyssey who kept Odysseus on her island.

clue.text: Worker accepts most of blame for trick

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a worker bee

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: guilt is blame or culpability

explanation.surface: An employee takes most of the blame for a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or deceive, to trick someone.

clue.text: Intake of breath: 75% nitrogen, say

indicators.note: 75% of a four-letter word is its first three, so the last is lost

parts.note: a gasp is a sudden intake of breath

explanation.surface: A breath of air is 75% nitrogen, give or take.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen is an example of a gas, the chief one in air.

clue.text: Rely on half of pool dropping a point

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the letter for the compass point is removed

parts.note: a swimming pool has a shallow end and a deep end
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone trusts half the pool, minus a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To depend on and to rely on are synonyms.

clue.text: Musical impresario records One in Ten

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A music promoter makes records with one in ten successes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Epstein managed the Beatles, the most famous pop impresario.
